gap: No result ChatGPT got states that the VIOFO A119M Pro's 62 Mb/s is H.264 while the 70mai A810S (29.4 Mb/s) and Vantrue S1 Pro Max (32 Mb/s) record H.265, so the 'half the bitrate' gap is the codec, and the VIOFO fills a card about twice as fast for it.
standout_why: Compared against the two cited pages (productbible.com, roadgearlab.com), tonyreviewsthings.com, pacificpartsdept.com, DashCamTalk's best-of list and our own front-and-rear page. RoadGearLab already has the raw bitrates (about 62 Mbps A119M Pro, about 29 + 10 Mbps A810S) and hours on a 256 GB card, but it says of its picks 'All use H.265' and that the 70mai writes 'roughly half what the VIOFO cameras write', with no codec caveat. DashCamTalk's spec page and Chuck McCoy's review thread both list the A119M Pro as H.264. Product Bible, Tony Reviews Things and Pacific Parts Dept give no bitrate or codec at all. So rivals hold the numbers but not the normalisation, and the one cited page that mentions codec has it wrong for the top pick.
decides: It confirms the VIOFO A119M Pro as an honest front-only pick but removes 'higher bitrate' as the reason, and it undoes ChatGPT's 'lower recording bitrate is a tradeoff' line against the 70mai. Put on one scale with ITU's 'half the bit rate' figure, the three sit within about 9% of each other (58.8 / 62 / 64 Mb/s H.264-equivalent). The real difference is card life: about 4.6 h of 4K on 128 GB for the VIOFO against about 8.9 h for a Vantrue S1 Pro Max front camera and about 9.7 h for the 70mai front alone. That makes the Vantrue S1 Pro Max 1CH (a partner-store product with no record yet, $135.99 when read 2026-11-21) a near-tie we can link, and it supports {after:vantrue-s1-pro-max-4k-2-5k} as the front-plus-rear row. One budget caveat: the A119M Pro is $209.99 at VIOFO's own US store today, so it is under $200 only at Amazon ($132.99 on DashCamTalk's tracker today) or Best Buy.

findings.label: Maximum bitrate before and after firmware V1.2_20260409, with file size
findings.value: 37 Mbps (267 MB per minute) at launch; 62 Mbps (445 MB per minute) after the firmware, H.264, 4K 30 fps

findings.note: Chuck McCoy's spec list in post 1, edited 'UPDATED JUNE 2, 2026 WITH FIRMWARE V1.2_20260409'. These are listed as 'Maximum Bitrate'; the thread does not describe how they were measured. A unit on older firmware writes 37 Mbps, not 62.

findings.label: Hours of 4K on a card (arithmetic)
findings.value: about 4.6 h on 128 GB, about 18.3 h on 512 GB (its maximum card)
findings.note: 62 Mb/s ÷ 8 × 3600 s = 27.9 GB per hour; 128 ÷ 27.9 = 4.6 h; 512 ÷ 27.9 = 18.3 h. Chuck McCoy's 445 MB per minute gives 26.7 GB per hour, or 4.8 h on 128 GB. Video only, decimal GB, card formatting overhead ignored.

findings.label: H.265 against H.264 at equal quality
findings.value: HEVC 'will need only half the bit rate of its predecessor' (H.264/AVC)
findings.source_title: New video codec to ease pressure on global networks (ITU, 25 January 2013)
findings.note: This is the standard's stated target, not a dash cam measurement. On that scale: 70mai 29.4 × 2 = 58.8, VIOFO 62 (already H.264), Vantrue 32 × 2 = 64 Mb/s H.264-equivalent, a spread of about 9%. At the VIOFO's launch 37 Mb/s it sat below both. Dealectric tests no units; real-time encoders may not reach the full gain.
